input.question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size
input.ground_truth: Hey there! I'm one of the bra fitting nazis over at /r/ABraThatFits, the community that produced that post you linked to, so I re-asked your question over there [and got some good answers if you want to check them out!](_URL_0_) It was super weird to see two of my favorite subreddits collide like this. Overall, however, there is not a lot of scholarship on the evolution of bras and bra sizing, which is sad, and I could probably spin you a nice little rant about sexism in academia, but I'm sure you can fill it in yourself. :) FYI, there isn't too much resistance in American brands against letters past D. No one does DDDD. Victoria's Secret goes D, DD, DDD, but lots of brands go D, DD, F, G, or D, DD, G, H. Take a look at two major US makers, Wacoal and Goddess, for examples of non-D sizing terminology. Lane Bryant, a major supplier of DD+ bras also does letters other than D. It's mostly just highly inconsistent, unlike the UK which has its stuff together.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a bunch of different sizes of shoes. But some shoe sizes don’t exist because the people who made the sizes a long time ago didn’t think those sizes were needed. The same thing happened with bra sizes in the U.S.

A long time ago, a company called brassiere makers (that means people who make bras) decided what sizes would be called “A,” “B,” “C,” and so on. They picked the sizes based on what they thought most people needed. But they forgot about some bigger sizes, like “D” and even bigger ones.

When women needed bras that were bigger than a “C,” the next size was called “D.” But the company that made the rules didn’t want to use the letter “E” or “F” for even bigger sizes, maybe because they thought those sizes were rare. So, instead of going up with letters, they started using “DD,” “DDD,” and so on. That’s why we have “DD” and “DDD”—because the letters just kept doubling up to show even bigger sizes!

So, the “DD” bra size happened because the old rules didn’t have enough letters for all the different sizes people need.
